title: Onboarding walkthrough GIFs + microcopy for rollout pin & fallback flows
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Create a set of onboarding assets for the Rollouts & Version Pinning surfaces to be used in the quickstart flow and docs. Deliverables include 3 short animated GIF walkthroughs (canary deploy, A/B split creation, fallback policy activation), a compact set of static PNGs for low-bandwidth docs, and a set of microcopy variants for the onboarding modal and success toast. Aim for progressive disclosure so new users see a single-line summary then can expand for details. Ensure keyboard/screen-reader friendly copy and two accessible color variants for public docs.
acceptance_criteria: Three animated GIFs (max 8s each) demonstrating end-to-end actions: create canary route, create A/B split, attach fallback policy
Two static PNG sequences (mobile and desktop widths) optimized for slow connections
Microcopy variants for modal header, short summary line, tooltip, and success toast with accessibility annotations
Figma file with exported frames + naming convention matching docs pipeline (rollout_canary_v1, rollout_ab_v1, rollout_fallback_v1)
Design reviewed and signed off by PM and at least one eng reviewer; accessibility checks documented
Assets uploaded to docs storage and PR in docs repo referencing asset URLs
comments: 2026-02-24 - Maya: Created ticket. Initial brief from PM (PM-398) attached. Goal is to make first-run experience for rollouts less intimidating for engineers evaluating pinning and fallback policies.
2026-02-26 - Liam: Kickoff — sketched three walkthrough ideas (inline tooltip, coachmark modal, combined stepper). Leaning toward short GIFs + expandable modal copy.
2026-02-28 - PM (Arnav Patel): Preference for progressive disclosure. Suggested showing only one critical CTA in the quickstart and surfacing advanced options in the docs.

2026-03-03 - Eng (Priya Kumar): Confirmed backend event names for telemetry we should highlight in the GIF (create_rollout, attach_fallback). Asked for 1-2 frame pause points so backend events are visible.
2026-03-06 - Accessibility review (Sara Li): Requested two color-contrast variants and alt-text templates for all GIFs; suggested 6s max length and a frame-level description for screen reader users.

2026-03-10 - Usability test (internal, n=6): Observations — users understood canary flow fastest when CTA labels matched console buttons; A/B was confusing without percentage labels. Action: add short percentage label overlays in the AB GIF.

2026-03-12 - Liam: Uploaded first drafts of GIFs to Drive and pushed preliminary assets to PR. Left TODOs in Figma for copy variants and mobile cropping. Next: iterate on timing and export high-contrast variants.
accessibility_notes: Provide alt-text file (plain text) for each GIF: summary + step timestamps
Ensure color contrast meets WCAG AA for body text and CTA overlays
Include keyboard-only flow screenshots for modal interactions
rollout_scenarios: Canary: Pin 5% traffic to new model variant, auto-promote after 1h if error_rate < 1%
A/B: 50/50 split created with explicit percentage overlays in UI
Fallback: Attach fallback to route that triggers model-variant swap on 503s
